frame: Parts are the MODEL'S (discovered functionally), names are OURS (CAS-PCBA types), ablation is the JUDGE. A label sticks only if its preregistered directional ablation prediction holds vs matched controls. This does NOT claim the model encodes CAS.
boundary: Bounded claim only. This run, at best, causally supports assigning CAS-PCBA type labels to specific internal parts of one pinned model under specific prompts, measures, and matched controls. It does not find 'the' neurons or 'the' circuit; it does not show the model encodes CAS; it does not establish that the measured directions carry drive semantics rather than topic/lexical content (CAS-specificity remains GREY per the matched-taxonomy lane); it does not license generation-control claims (cite Stage 27P for the eraser channel, two families only); it does not transfer to other models, layers, hook points, or prompt distributions without rerunning. Rev 0.4 is judged on a DIFFERENT model (EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b) from rev 0.3 (pythia-2.8b) and rev 0.2 (pythia-1b); it does not amend or supersede the rev-0.2 NULL_ATLAS_V0 or the rev-0.3 GREY_ATLAS_V0_INSUFFICIENT_EVALUABLE result, both of which stand as reported. Rev 0.4 additionally runs in bfloat16 (deviation D33), so any effect whose relative size is at or below the bf16 quantum is reported as BELOW THE INSTRUMENT'S RESOLUTION and its null is UNINFORMATIVE, not evidence.
aggregate_caveat: The five core tests are NOT independent: DR-F5, AMP-F5, and CONN share the F5 judge bank and the u_F5 direction; DR-F5 and DR-F2 share method. The pass fraction is DESCRIPTIVE ONLY; no binomial p-value is licensed as a headline. Per-test evidence (each against its own matched controls) is the primary result. Better power in rev 0.3 does not change this: the tests are non-independent BY DESIGN, not by sample size.
rev03_provenance_note: Rev 0.3 design changes were made AFTER seeing the rev-0.2 NULL result and are therefore informed by rev-0.2 outcomes. They are legitimate iteration, NOT post-hoc tuning, ONLY because (a) every change is logged with date and reason in PREREG section 10 BEFORE any rev-0.3 run, and (b) rev 0.3 is judged on a different model with re-drawn banks. The rev-0.2 result is reported unamended.
rev04_provenance_note: Rev 0.4 is INFORMED BY REV-0.2 AND REV-0.3 OUTCOMES. The AMP readout change (D35), the control-construction rebuild (D37-D39), the dropped DR-F2 rail (D40) and the CHECK-informed reading of the battery were all chosen AFTER seeing rev 0.3's GREY_ATLAS_V0_INSUFFICIENT_EVALUABLE. That is legitimate iteration, NOT post-hoc tuning, ONLY because (a) every change is logged with date and reason in PREREG section 10 BEFORE any rev-0.4 run, and (b) rev 0.4 is judged on a DIFFERENT model (EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b). The rev-0.2 and rev-0.3 results are reported unamended. Note explicitly that dropping the DR-F2 rail is justified PARTLY BY REV-0.3 OUTCOMES (behavioural change 0.313, targeted drop 0.00132, 48x below the bf16 quantum) and is declared as such rather than presented as independent design. SECOND PASS (2026-08-19, still before any rev-0.4 run): an adversarial review of the rev-0.4 draft found that several of D32-D45 were not actually delivered by the draft as written -- the probe readout had no viability gate and simultaneously disabled the D41 pass window, the D39 damage guard and the C=20 floor were mutually defeating, the dose match was reported but gated on nothing, the measurability floor was misderived, and the battery did not fit the window once the calibration and preflight were counted. D46-D55 repair the draft; they are defect fixes against the design already logged, not new science, and they are logged BEFORE any pod time is spent.
measurability_note: bfloat16 carries 8 significand bits, i.e. a RAW relative quantum of 2^-8 = 3.90625e-3. That raw figure is NOT the binding floor and rev 0.4's first draft misused it (deviation D52): every judged quantity here is a mean over ~n_prompts x n_continuation_positions measurements, and independent quantization noise averages down by sqrt(n), so the EFFECTIVE quantization floor is roughly 32x smaller at n ~ 1024. The BINDING floor is the statistical standard error (0.2662 on the rev-0.3 AMP projection, ~25x the quantization scale). An effect at or below the EFFECTIVE quantization floor is BELOW THE INSTRUMENT'S RESOLUTION at this dtype: its null is UNINFORMATIVE and may not be read as evidence of absence, and in rev 0.4's second pass it also blocks a PASS rather than merely labelling a null. The statistical floor is reported but is NEVER used to reclassify a genuine statistical null as UNINFORMATIVE -- the paired p-values already handle it. Continuous measurements survive bf16 WEIGHTS only because every measurement path is forced to fp32 (see provenance.precision_policy) and every comparison is PAIRED, so systematic bf16 bias cancels between baseline and condition on the same prompts. The DISCRETE risk does not cancel: greedy argmax can resolve differently at near-ties, which inflates behavioral_change_rate and destroys byte-identity tie structure. That is what the D34 pythia-2.8b bf16-vs-fp32 calibration exists to measure, and it must be read before this report's VACUOUS preconditions are taken at face value.

precision_policy.rationale: bf16 WEIGHTS with fp32 measurement math. The bf16 dot-product error over 6144 dims with fp32 accumulation is 1.44e-5 x ||h||, i.e. negligible -- but ONLY if accumulation is forced, which is why allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction is pinned False. The lm-head island matters because greedy argmax, the hedge probability MASS and the CHECK gate score in nats all read the logits, where bf16 error near |logit| = 15 is a ~6% multiplicative error per softmax probability.
precision_policy.residual_discrete_risk: argmax flips at near-ties do NOT cancel under pairing. They inflate behavioral_change_rate and destroy the byte-identity tie structure that D9/D23/D29 depend on, which could flip a VACUOUS precondition to evaluable on numerical noise. This is what the D34 pythia-2.8b bf16-vs-fp32 calibration measures.
